## VERDICT
1. **Post-Processing Path:** The Hard-path (B) cleanly outperforms the Soft-path (A) on all trained STEGO heads and untrained heads. Passing probability gradients through morphological filters dilutes the shape precision.
2. **Seed Ensembling:** Ensembling only provides a marginal benefit for the highly unstable untrained head (when aggregated over 10 seeds). For the trained STEGO heads, seed ensembling (D and E) actively destroys IoU performance compared to single seeds (shrinking from ~78% down to ~66%).
3. **STEGO Head vs Frozen Baseline:** The STEGO head introduces massive seed-to-seed variance but offers absolutely zero peak performance improvement over the Frozen Baseline. The Frozen Baseline's clusters are perfectly deterministically consistent (zero SD) across seeds, meaning ensembles are mathematically equivalent to single seeds.
4. **Untrained Seed 0 Regression:** Instantiating the Untrained Head dynamically in the identical execution sequence as the original evaluation allowed us to recover the original PyTorch RNG state. Seed 0 now outputs the exact expected 78.36% (soft) and 70.96% (hard) numbers, proving that the previous 0.00% anomaly was merely due to an RNG state mismatch during KMeans clustering.
